title: Elevation Health Assessment Tool
description: Healthcare Technology Evaluation Assessment with 49 questions across 4 categories

steps.title: Reimbursement
steps.description: Evaluate payor-based reimbursement strategies, virtual care services, and FDA regulatory requirements
steps.helpText: This section evaluates your company's approach to healthcare reimbursement, including payor relationships, virtual care capabilities, and regulatory compliance.

reference.title: CMS Reimbursement Guidelines
reference.description: Official CMS guidelines for healthcare reimbursement strategies

q1_payor_reimbursement.title: Does the Company's business model rely on payor-based reimbursement? (If not, skip to Question 6.) If so, is there evidence of payors providing reimbursement for the type of services outlined in this Company's business model?
q1_payor_reimbursement.subCategory: Annual Physician Fee Updates and Reimbursement Codes

Yes.rationale: Strong reimbursement foundation indicates high market viability and low financial risk

Maybe.rationale: Uncertain reimbursement pathway requires strengthening but shows potential

No.rationale: Alternative revenue model (direct-pay, employer-based) can be equally viable - reroutes to different investment lens

q1_payor_reimbursement.helpText: Payor-based reimbursement is critical for sustainable healthcare technology adoption. Consider Medicare, Medicaid, and private insurance coverage.
q1_payor_reimbursement.explanation: A 'No' answer doesn't indicate low viability—it redirects evaluation to alternative revenue models like direct-to-consumer, employer-based, or subscription models.

q2_reimbursement_strategy.title: If the Company should have a reimbursement strategy, have they provided documentation to lay out their strategy?
q2_reimbursement_strategy.subCategory: Annual Physician Fee Updates and Reimbursement Codes

Yes.rationale: Documented strategy demonstrates high readiness and low risk

Maybe.rationale: Partial documentation indicates moderate readiness, needs strengthening

No.rationale: Lack of documentation presents high risk and gaps in planning

q2_reimbursement_strategy.helpText: A documented reimbursement strategy demonstrates market understanding and business planning maturity.
q2_reimbursement_strategy.explanation: Comprehensive reimbursement documentation should include CPT codes, coverage policies, and payor engagement strategies.

q2_reimbursement_documentation.title: Please upload reimbursement strategy documentation
q2_reimbursement_documentation.helpText: Upload your reimbursement strategy document, business plan, or payor analysis.
q2_reimbursement_documentation.explanation: Documentation provides evidence of strategic planning and market analysis.

uploaded.rationale: Documentation upload demonstrates transparency and preparation

not_uploaded.rationale: No penalty for missing optional documentation

q3_reimbursement_red_flags.title: If the Company does have a reimbursement strategy, are there any potential red flags in the reimbursement strategy that they present? (If there are potential issues, please provide a couple of lines in the notes section - Column K.)
q3_reimbursement_red_flags.subCategory: Annual Physician Fee Updates and Reimbursement Codes

no_red_flags.rationale: No identified red flags indicates high readiness and low risk

minor_concerns.rationale: Minor concerns present moderate risk, needs strengthening

major_concerns.rationale: Major red flags present high risk and significant gaps

q3_reimbursement_red_flags.helpText: Common red flags include unrealistic reimbursement assumptions, lack of payor engagement, or misunderstanding of coverage policies.
q3_reimbursement_red_flags.explanation: Identifying potential issues early helps mitigate risks and improve strategy development.
q3_reimbursement_red_flags.placeholder: Describe any concerns or red flags in the reimbursement strategy...

q4_cpt_codes.title: Does the Company have a plan to obtain new CPT codes or use existing CPT codes?
q4_cpt_codes.subCategory: Annual Physician Fee Updates and Reimbursement Codes

Existing CPT codes.rationale: Existing CPT codes provide immediate reimbursement pathway with low risk

Both.rationale: Hybrid approach demonstrates high readiness and strategic planning

New CPT codes.rationale: New CPT codes show innovation but need strengthening in timeline planning

Uncertain.rationale: Uncertainty indicates high risk and gaps in reimbursement planning

q4_cpt_codes.helpText: CPT codes are essential for billing and reimbursement. New codes require AMA approval and can take 2-3 years.
q4_cpt_codes.explanation: Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes are necessary for healthcare billing and reimbursement processes.

reference.title: AMA CPT Code Application Process
reference.description: Official process for obtaining new CPT codes

q5_cpt_timeline.title: What is the timeline for CPT code implementation?
q5_cpt_timeline.subCategory: Annual Physician Fee Updates and Reimbursement Codes

Already implemented.rationale: Implementation complete indicates high readiness and low risk

6-12 months.rationale: Moderate timeline shows good planning but needs strengthening

1-2 years.rationale: Longer timeline acceptable for new CPT codes but requires monitoring

2-3 years.rationale: Extended timeline presents high risk and market entry delays

3+ years.rationale: Very long timeline indicates high risk and significant gaps

q5_cpt_timeline.helpText: CPT code timelines vary significantly based on complexity and AMA review processes.
q5_cpt_timeline.explanation: Understanding implementation timelines is crucial for business planning and revenue projections.

q6_virtual_care.title: Does the Company provide virtual care services?

Yes.rationale: Virtual care services demonstrate high market readiness and low risk

Planning to.rationale: Planning shows awareness but needs strengthening in implementation

No.rationale: Not providing virtual care may limit market opportunities but acceptable for some models

q6_virtual_care.helpText: Virtual care services have specific reimbursement considerations and regulatory requirements.
q6_virtual_care.explanation: Telehealth and virtual care services require compliance with state licensing, HIPAA, and reimbursement policies.

reference.title: CMS Telehealth Services
reference.description: Medicare telehealth coverage and payment policies

q7_telehealth_compliance.title: Are virtual care services compliant with state licensing and telehealth regulations?

Fully compliant.rationale: Full compliance indicates high readiness and low regulatory risk

Partially compliant.rationale: Partial compliance shows progress but needs strengthening

Under review.rationale: Review process shows awareness but creates moderate risk

Non-compliant.rationale: Non-compliance presents high risk and significant gaps

q7_telehealth_compliance.helpText: State licensing requirements vary significantly for telehealth services across different states.
q7_telehealth_compliance.explanation: Compliance with state-specific telehealth regulations is mandatory for legal operation.

q8_fda_clearance.title: Does the Company's technology require FDA clearance or approval?

No.rationale: No FDA requirement indicates high readiness and low regulatory risk

Yes - 510(k).rationale: 510(k) pathway is established but needs strengthening in execution

Yes - De Novo.rationale: De Novo pathway shows innovation but requires careful management

Yes - PMA.rationale: PMA pathway presents high risk and significant regulatory gaps

Uncertain.rationale: Regulatory uncertainty creates high risk and planning gaps

q8_fda_clearance.helpText: FDA classification determines regulatory pathway and impacts reimbursement eligibility.
q8_fda_clearance.explanation: Medical devices and software often require FDA clearance before market entry and reimbursement consideration.

reference.title: FDA Medical Device Classification
reference.description: FDA guidance on medical device classification and regulatory pathways

q8_fda_documentation.title: Please upload FDA submission documentation or regulatory strategy
q8_fda_documentation.helpText: Upload FDA submission materials, pre-submission feedback, or regulatory strategy documents.
q8_fda_documentation.explanation: FDA documentation demonstrates regulatory planning and compliance preparation.

q9_fda_timeline.title: What is the expected timeline for FDA clearance/approval?

Already approved.rationale: FDA approval complete indicates high readiness and low risk

6-12 months.rationale: Moderate timeline acceptable but needs strengthening in execution

1-2 years.rationale: Longer timeline manageable with proper planning

2+ years.rationale: Extended timeline presents high risk and market entry delays

q9_fda_timeline.helpText: FDA review timelines vary by device classification and submission quality.
q9_fda_timeline.explanation: Accurate timeline estimation is crucial for business planning and investor expectations.

q10_clinical_evidence.title: Does the Company have clinical evidence supporting efficacy and safety?

Extensive clinical data.rationale: Extensive clinical evidence demonstrates high readiness and low risk

Limited clinical data.rationale: Limited data provides foundation but needs strengthening

Preclinical data only.rationale: Preclinical only presents high risk and significant evidence gaps

No clinical data.rationale: No clinical evidence presents high risk and major gaps

q10_clinical_evidence.helpText: Clinical evidence is essential for FDA approval and payor coverage decisions.
q10_clinical_evidence.explanation: Robust clinical evidence demonstrates safety, efficacy, and value proposition to stakeholders.

q10_clinical_documentation.title: Please upload clinical study reports or evidence summaries
q10_clinical_documentation.helpText: Upload clinical study reports, white papers, or evidence summaries.
q10_clinical_documentation.explanation: Clinical documentation provides evidence of safety and efficacy claims.

q11_health_economics.title: Has the Company conducted health economics and outcomes research (HEOR)?

Comprehensive HEOR.rationale: Comprehensive HEOR demonstrates strong value proposition and low risk

Basic cost analysis.rationale: Basic analysis provides foundation but needs strengthening

Planned but not started.rationale: Planning shows awareness but presents high risk without execution

No HEOR conducted.rationale: No HEOR presents significant gaps in value demonstration

q11_health_economics.helpText: HEOR studies demonstrate economic value and support reimbursement negotiations.
q11_health_economics.explanation: Health economics research quantifies the value proposition and cost-effectiveness of healthcare technologies.

q12_market_access.title: Does the Company have a market access strategy?

Comprehensive strategy.rationale: Comprehensive strategy indicates high readiness and low market risk

Basic strategy.rationale: Basic strategy provides foundation but needs strengthening

In development.rationale: Development shows awareness but creates moderate risk

No strategy.rationale: No strategy presents high risk and significant market access gaps

q12_market_access.helpText: Market access strategy outlines pathways to coverage and reimbursement.
q12_market_access.explanation: Effective market access strategies address payor needs, evidence requirements, and value communication.

q13_payor_engagement.title: Has the Company engaged with payors regarding coverage policies?

Active engagement.rationale: Active engagement demonstrates high readiness and low coverage risk

Initial discussions.rationale: Initial discussions show progress but need strengthening

Planned engagement.rationale: Planning shows awareness but creates moderate risk

No engagement.rationale: No engagement presents high risk and significant coverage gaps

q13_payor_engagement.helpText: Early payor engagement helps understand coverage requirements and evidence needs.
q13_payor_engagement.explanation: Proactive payor engagement improves likelihood of favorable coverage decisions.

q14_coverage_gap.title: Are there existing coverage gaps that the technology addresses?

Significant gaps.rationale: Addressing significant gaps provides strong value proposition and low risk

Moderate gaps.rationale: Moderate gaps provide value but need strengthening in positioning

Minor gaps.rationale: Minor gaps provide some value but limited differentiation

No gaps identified.rationale: No identified gaps presents high risk in value demonstration

q14_coverage_gap.helpText: Addressing coverage gaps strengthens the value proposition for payors.
q14_coverage_gap.explanation: Technologies that fill coverage gaps have stronger reimbursement potential.

q15_competitive_analysis.title: Has the Company analyzed competitor reimbursement strategies?

Comprehensive analysis.rationale: Comprehensive analysis demonstrates high market understanding and low risk

Basic analysis.rationale: Basic analysis provides foundation but needs strengthening

In progress.rationale: Progress shows awareness but creates moderate risk

No analysis.rationale: No analysis presents high risk and market knowledge gaps

q15_competitive_analysis.helpText: Understanding competitor strategies informs positioning and differentiation.
q15_competitive_analysis.explanation: Competitive analysis reveals market dynamics and successful reimbursement approaches.

q16_pricing_strategy.title: Does the Company have a pricing strategy aligned with reimbursement rates?

Fully aligned.rationale: Full alignment demonstrates high readiness and low pricing risk

Partially aligned.rationale: Partial alignment shows progress but needs strengthening

Under development.rationale: Development shows awareness but creates moderate risk

Not aligned.rationale: Misalignment presents high risk and adoption barriers

q16_pricing_strategy.helpText: Pricing must consider reimbursement rates to ensure provider adoption.
q16_pricing_strategy.explanation: Sustainable pricing strategies balance profitability with market accessibility.

q17_risk_mitigation.title: What risk mitigation strategies are in place for reimbursement challenges?

comprehensive_strategy.rationale: Comprehensive risk mitigation demonstrates high preparedness and low risk

basic_strategy.rationale: Basic strategy shows awareness but needs strengthening

limited_strategy.rationale: Limited strategy presents high risk and planning gaps

q17_risk_mitigation.helpText: Risk mitigation strategies should address regulatory, coverage, and competitive risks.
q17_risk_mitigation.explanation: Proactive risk management demonstrates business maturity and planning sophistication.
q17_risk_mitigation.placeholder: Describe risk mitigation strategies for reimbursement challenges...

q18_reimbursement_timeline.title: What is the expected timeline to achieve sustainable reimbursement?

0-6 months.rationale: Short timeline indicates high readiness and low implementation risk

6-12 months.rationale: Reasonable timeline demonstrates good planning and low risk

1-2 years.rationale: Moderate timeline acceptable but needs strengthening in execution

2-3 years.rationale: Longer timeline manageable with proper milestones

3+ years.rationale: Extended timeline presents high risk and market entry delays

q18_reimbursement_timeline.helpText: Realistic timelines consider regulatory approval, evidence generation, and payor negotiations.
q18_reimbursement_timeline.explanation: Timeline expectations should align with regulatory pathways and market dynamics.

steps.title: Privacy & Data Access
steps.description: Assess HIPAA compliance, information blocking rules, and data privacy regulations
steps.helpText: This section evaluates your organization's compliance with healthcare privacy regulations, data access requirements, and information blocking rules.

reference.title: HHS HIPAA Security Rule
reference.description: Official HIPAA Security Rule guidance and requirements

validation.completionMessage: Privacy and data access assessment completed successfully

q19_hipaa_entity.title: If the Company is a CE or a BA and handling PHI (collecting, storing, exchanging, providing access), does the Company have a dedicated senior-level officer to handle data privacy and data security issues?

Yes.rationale: Dedicated privacy officer ensures HIPAA compliance and accountability

No.rationale: Lack of dedicated officer creates compliance risk

Not applicable.rationale: Not handling PHI reduces regulatory burden

q19_hipaa_entity.helpText: HIPAA requires covered entities and business associates to have appropriate administrative safeguards including designated security officials.
q19_hipaa_entity.explanation: A dedicated privacy/security officer ensures compliance oversight and accountability for PHI protection.

q19_privacy_officer_credentials.title: Please upload privacy officer credentials or organizational chart
q19_privacy_officer_credentials.helpText: Upload privacy officer resume, certifications, or organizational structure.

uploaded.rationale: Privacy officer credentials demonstrate qualified leadership

q20_data_governance.title: Does the Company have a comprehensive data governance framework?

Comprehensive framework.rationale: Comprehensive framework ensures high data management readiness and low risk

Basic framework.rationale: Basic framework provides foundation but needs strengthening

In development.rationale: Development shows awareness but creates moderate risk

No framework.rationale: No framework presents high risk and governance gaps

q20_data_governance.helpText: Data governance frameworks establish policies, procedures, and controls for data management throughout its lifecycle.
q20_data_governance.explanation: Effective data governance ensures data quality, security, privacy, and regulatory compliance.

q21_encryption.title: Is PHI encrypted both at rest and in transit?
enum: Both at rest and in transit

Both at rest and in transit.rationale: Complete encryption provides maximum PHI protection and low risk

At rest only.rationale: Partial encryption leaves data vulnerable during transmission

In transit only.rationale: Partial encryption leaves stored data vulnerable

No encryption.rationale: No encryption creates significant security risk

q21_encryption.helpText: HIPAA requires encryption of PHI to prevent unauthorized access during storage and transmission.
q21_encryption.explanation: Encryption is a critical technical safeguard that protects PHI from unauthorized disclosure.

q21_encryption_certificate.title: Please upload encryption implementation documentation or security certificates
q21_encryption_certificate.helpText: Upload encryption specifications, SSL certificates, or security audit reports.

q21_encryption: Both at rest and in transit

q22_access_controls.title: Are there role-based access controls for PHI?

Comprehensive RBAC.rationale: Comprehensive RBAC ensures proper access control and low risk

Basic access controls.rationale: Basic controls provide foundation but need strengthening

No access controls.rationale: No controls create significant security risk

q22_access_controls.helpText: Role-based access controls ensure that only authorized individuals can access PHI based on their job functions.
q22_access_controls.explanation: RBAC implements the principle of least privilege, limiting access to the minimum necessary for job functions.

q23_audit_logs.title: Does the system maintain comprehensive audit logs for PHI access?

Comprehensive logging.rationale: Comprehensive logging ensures full audit trail and low risk

Basic logging.rationale: Basic logging provides foundation but needs strengthening

Limited logging.rationale: Limited logging creates moderate compliance risk

No logging.rationale: No logging creates significant compliance risk

q23_audit_logs.helpText: Audit logs track all PHI access and modifications to detect unauthorized use and support compliance monitoring.
q23_audit_logs.explanation: HIPAA requires audit controls to record access and other activity in information systems containing PHI.

q24_breach_response.title: Is there a documented breach response plan?

Comprehensive plan.rationale: Comprehensive breach response plan ensures rapid incident management

Basic plan.rationale: Basic plan provides foundation but may need enhancement

In development.rationale: Plan development shows awareness but lacks implementation

No plan.rationale: No breach response plan creates significant compliance risk

q24_breach_response.helpText: HIPAA requires covered entities to have procedures for responding to security incidents and breaches.
q24_breach_response.explanation: Breach response plans ensure rapid detection, containment, and notification of security incidents.

q24_breach_response_plan.title: Please upload breach response plan documentation
q24_breach_response_plan.helpText: Upload breach response procedures, incident response plan, or security policies.
q24_breach_response_plan.explanation: Documentation demonstrates preparedness for security incidents.

uploaded.rationale: Breach response documentation demonstrates incident preparedness

q25_employee_training.title: Do all employees receive regular HIPAA and privacy training?

Regular comprehensive training.rationale: Regular training ensures workforce compliance and low risk

Basic training.rationale: Basic training provides foundation but needs strengthening

Irregular training.rationale: Irregular training creates moderate compliance risk

No training.rationale: No training creates significant compliance risk

q25_employee_training.helpText: HIPAA requires workforce training on privacy and security policies and procedures.
q25_employee_training.explanation: Regular training ensures employees understand their responsibilities for protecting PHI.

q26_information_blocking.title: Is the Company compliant with information blocking regulations?

Fully compliant.rationale: Full compliance ensures patient access rights and low regulatory risk

Mostly compliant.rationale: Mostly compliant shows progress but needs strengthening

Partially compliant.rationale: Partial compliance creates moderate regulatory risk

q26_information_blocking.helpText: Information blocking regulations require healthcare providers and technology developers to support patient access to health information.
q26_information_blocking.explanation: The 21st Century Cures Act prohibits information blocking practices that interfere with patient access to health information.

reference.title: ONC Information Blocking Rule
reference.description: Official guidance on information blocking regulations

q27_patient_access.title: Does the system provide patients with easy access to their health information?

Full patient portal access.rationale: Full patient access ensures compliance and patient empowerment

Limited access.rationale: Limited access provides foundation but needs strengthening

Request-based access.rationale: Request-based access meets minimum requirements but creates barriers

No patient access.rationale: No patient access creates significant compliance risk

q27_patient_access.helpText: Patients have the right to access their PHI under HIPAA and information blocking regulations.
q27_patient_access.explanation: Patient access to health information improves care coordination and patient engagement.

q28_data_portability.title: Does the system support data portability and export capabilities?

Full portability.rationale: Full portability ensures patient rights and reduces information blocking risk

Limited portability.rationale: Limited portability provides foundation but needs strengthening

Export only.rationale: Export capability meets basic requirements but limits functionality

No portability.rationale: No portability creates information blocking risk

q28_data_portability.helpText: Data portability enables patients and providers to move health information between systems.
q28_data_portability.explanation: Interoperability and data portability reduce information blocking and improve care coordination.

q29_consent_management.title: Is there a robust consent management system for data sharing?

Comprehensive consent management.rationale: Comprehensive consent management ensures patient autonomy and low risk

Basic consent tracking.rationale: Basic tracking provides foundation but needs strengthening

Manual consent process.rationale: Manual process meets requirements but creates operational risk

No consent management.rationale: No consent management creates significant compliance risk

q29_consent_management.helpText: Consent management systems track patient preferences for data sharing and use.
q29_consent_management.explanation: Proper consent management ensures patient autonomy and regulatory compliance.

q30_third_party_sharing.title: Are there controls for third-party data sharing agreements?

Comprehensive controls.rationale: Comprehensive controls ensure proper third-party management and low risk

Basic agreements.rationale: Basic agreements provide foundation but need strengthening

Limited oversight.rationale: Limited oversight creates moderate compliance risk

No controls.rationale: No controls create significant compliance risk

q30_third_party_sharing.helpText: Business associate agreements and data sharing controls are required for third-party PHI access.
q30_third_party_sharing.explanation: Third-party data sharing requires appropriate safeguards and contractual protections.

q31_privacy_impact.title: Has the Company conducted privacy impact assessments?

Comprehensive PIAs.rationale: Comprehensive PIAs demonstrate proactive privacy management and low risk

Basic assessments.rationale: Basic assessments provide foundation but need strengthening

Planned assessments.rationale: Planning shows awareness but creates moderate risk

No assessments.rationale: No assessments create significant privacy risk

q31_privacy_impact.helpText: Privacy impact assessments identify and mitigate privacy risks in systems and processes.
q31_privacy_impact.explanation: PIAs help organizations proactively address privacy concerns and regulatory requirements.

q32_data_minimization.title: Does the Company implement data minimization principles?

Strict minimization.rationale: Strict minimization ensures compliance and reduces privacy risk

General minimization.rationale: General minimization provides foundation but needs strengthening

Limited minimization.rationale: Limited minimization creates moderate privacy risk

No minimization.rationale: No minimization creates significant privacy risk

q32_data_minimization.helpText: Data minimization limits collection and use of PHI to the minimum necessary for intended purposes.
q32_data_minimization.explanation: The minimum necessary standard is a core HIPAA requirement for PHI use and disclosure.

q33_retention_policies.title: Are there documented data retention and disposal policies?

Comprehensive policies.rationale: Comprehensive policies ensure proper data lifecycle management and low risk

Basic policies.rationale: Basic policies provide foundation but need strengthening

In development.rationale: Development shows awareness but creates moderate risk

No policies.rationale: No policies create significant compliance risk

q33_retention_policies.helpText: Data retention policies specify how long PHI is kept and how it is securely disposed of when no longer needed.
q33_retention_policies.explanation: Proper data lifecycle management reduces privacy risks and ensures regulatory compliance.

q34_international_compliance.title: If operating internationally, is the Company compliant with applicable privacy laws (GDPR, etc.)?

Fully compliant.rationale: Full international compliance demonstrates global readiness and low risk

Mostly compliant.rationale: Mostly compliant shows progress but needs strengthening

Partially compliant.rationale: Partial compliance creates moderate regulatory risk

Not applicable.rationale: Not operating internationally reduces regulatory complexity

q34_international_compliance.helpText: International operations may require compliance with additional privacy regulations like GDPR.
q34_international_compliance.explanation: Global privacy regulations have varying requirements for data protection and patient rights.

q35_vendor_management.title: Is there a vendor risk management program for privacy and security?

Comprehensive program.rationale: Comprehensive vendor management ensures third-party compliance and low risk

Basic assessments.rationale: Basic assessments provide foundation but need strengthening

Limited oversight.rationale: Limited oversight creates moderate vendor risk

No program.rationale: No program creates significant vendor risk

q35_vendor_management.helpText: Vendor risk management ensures third-party service providers meet privacy and security requirements.
q35_vendor_management.explanation: Business associates must provide appropriate safeguards for PHI under HIPAA requirements.

q36_privacy_by_design.title: Does the Company implement privacy by design principles?

Comprehensive implementation.rationale: Comprehensive privacy by design ensures proactive protection and low risk

Basic implementation.rationale: Basic implementation provides foundation but needs strengthening

Planned implementation.rationale: Planning shows awareness but creates moderate risk

No implementation.rationale: No implementation creates significant privacy risk

q36_privacy_by_design.helpText: Privacy by design integrates privacy considerations into system design and development processes.
q36_privacy_by_design.explanation: Proactive privacy protection is more effective and cost-efficient than reactive compliance.

q37_privacy_complaints.title: Is there a process for handling privacy complaints and requests?

Formal process.rationale: Formal process ensures proper complaint handling and low compliance risk

Informal process.rationale: Informal process provides foundation but needs strengthening

Ad-hoc handling.rationale: Ad-hoc handling creates moderate compliance risk

No process.rationale: No process creates significant compliance risk

q37_privacy_complaints.helpText: HIPAA requires covered entities to have procedures for individuals to file complaints about privacy practices.
q37_privacy_complaints.explanation: Effective complaint handling demonstrates commitment to privacy protection and regulatory compliance.

steps.title: Data Interoperability
steps.description: Review FHIR standards, API requirements, and interoperability policies
steps.helpText: This section evaluates your system's ability to exchange and use health information across different healthcare organizations and technology platforms.

reference.title: HL7 FHIR Standards
reference.description: Official HL7 FHIR specification and implementation guides

q38_fhir_compliance.title: If the Company uses and shares patient data with CAH or eligible hospital clients through an EHR, is the EHR a Certified EHR Technology (CEHRT)?

Yes.rationale: CEHRT certification ensures interoperability and CMS program eligibility

No.rationale: Non-certified EHR limits CMS program participation and interoperability

Not applicable.rationale: Not using EHR reduces certification requirements

q38_fhir_compliance.helpText: CEHRT certification ensures EHR systems meet interoperability and security requirements for CMS programs.
q38_fhir_compliance.explanation: Certified EHR Technology is required for participation in CMS quality programs and meaningful use incentives.

reference.title: ONC Health IT Certification Program
reference.description: Official certification requirements for health IT systems

q38_cehrt_certificate.title: Please upload CEHRT certification documentation
q38_cehrt_certificate.helpText: Upload CEHRT certification letter or ONC-ACB documentation.
q38_cehrt_certificate.explanation: Certification documentation validates EHR compliance claims.

q39_fhir_implementation.title: Does the system implement HL7 FHIR standards for data exchange?

FHIR R4.rationale: FHIR R4 is the current standard for modern interoperability and low risk

FHIR STU3.rationale: FHIR STU3 provides good interoperability but should upgrade to R4

Earlier FHIR version.rationale: Earlier FHIR versions have limited interoperability capabilities

No FHIR implementation.rationale: No FHIR implementation limits modern interoperability significantly

q39_fhir_implementation.helpText: FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) is the modern standard for healthcare data exchange.
q39_fhir_implementation.explanation: FHIR R4 is the current standard required for 21st Century Cures Act compliance and modern interoperability.

q39_fhir_documentation.title: Please upload FHIR implementation guide or API documentation
q39_fhir_documentation.helpText: Upload FHIR implementation guide, API documentation, or capability statements.
q39_fhir_documentation.explanation: FHIR documentation demonstrates technical implementation details.

q40_api_capabilities.title: Does the system provide standardized APIs for data access?

FHIR APIs.rationale: FHIR APIs provide modern standardized access and low interoperability risk

RESTful APIs.rationale: RESTful APIs provide good access but need FHIR standardization

Legacy APIs.rationale: Legacy APIs provide limited interoperability capabilities

No APIs.rationale: No APIs create significant interoperability barriers

q40_api_capabilities.helpText: Standardized APIs enable secure, authorized access to patient data by third-party applications.
q40_api_capabilities.explanation: The 21st Century Cures Act requires certified health IT to support standardized APIs for patient access.

q41_data_standards.title: Which clinical data standards does the system support?

SNOMED CT.rationale: SNOMED CT provides comprehensive clinical terminology support

LOINC.rationale: LOINC provides essential laboratory and clinical observation standards

ICD-10.rationale: ICD-10 provides basic diagnosis coding support

None.rationale: No clinical standards support creates significant interoperability gaps

q41_data_standards.helpText: Clinical data standards ensure consistent representation and exchange of health information.
q41_data_standards.explanation: Standardized clinical terminologies enable semantic interoperability across healthcare systems.

q42_care_coordination.title: Does the system support care coordination workflows?

Comprehensive workflows.rationale: Comprehensive workflows enable effective care coordination and low risk

Basic workflows.rationale: Basic workflows provide foundation but need strengthening

Limited support.rationale: Limited support creates moderate care coordination barriers

No support.rationale: No support creates significant care coordination gaps

q42_care_coordination.helpText: Care coordination workflows facilitate communication and information sharing among healthcare providers.
q42_care_coordination.explanation: Effective care coordination improves patient outcomes and reduces healthcare costs.

q43_patient_matching.title: Does the system implement patient matching capabilities?

Advanced matching algorithms.rationale: Advanced algorithms ensure accurate patient identification and low safety risk

Basic matching.rationale: Basic matching provides foundation but needs strengthening

Manual matching.rationale: Manual matching creates moderate efficiency and accuracy risks

No matching.rationale: No matching creates significant patient safety risks

q43_patient_matching.helpText: Patient matching ensures health information is correctly associated with the right patient across systems.
q43_patient_matching.explanation: Accurate patient matching is critical for patient safety and care continuity.

q44_quality_reporting.title: Does the system support automated quality measure reporting?

Automated reporting.rationale: Automated reporting reduces provider burden and improves accuracy

Semi-automated.rationale: Semi-automated provides foundation but needs full automation

Manual reporting.rationale: Manual reporting creates efficiency and accuracy challenges

No reporting.rationale: No reporting creates significant CMS program participation barriers

q44_quality_reporting.helpText: Automated quality reporting reduces provider burden and improves data accuracy for CMS programs.
q44_quality_reporting.explanation: Quality measure reporting is required for various CMS quality programs and value-based care initiatives.

q45_health_information_exchange.title: Does the system participate in Health Information Exchanges (HIEs)?

Active HIE participation.rationale: Active HIE participation enables comprehensive care coordination

Limited participation.rationale: Limited participation provides foundation but needs expansion

Planned participation.rationale: Planning shows awareness but creates moderate interoperability gaps

No participation.rationale: No participation creates significant care coordination barriers

q45_health_information_exchange.helpText: HIE participation enables sharing of patient information across different healthcare organizations.
q45_health_information_exchange.explanation: HIEs improve care coordination and reduce duplicate testing and procedures.

q46_interoperability_testing.title: Has the system undergone interoperability testing and validation?

Comprehensive testing.rationale: Comprehensive testing ensures reliable interoperability and low implementation risk

Basic testing.rationale: Basic testing provides foundation but needs comprehensive validation

Planned testing.rationale: Planning shows awareness but creates moderate implementation risk

No testing.rationale: No testing creates significant interoperability implementation risk

q46_interoperability_testing.helpText: Interoperability testing validates that systems can successfully exchange and use health information.
q46_interoperability_testing.explanation: Testing ensures that interoperability implementations work correctly in real-world scenarios.
